'''''Agave weberi''''', known as '''maguey liso''' in Spanish and as '''Weber's agave''' in English, is a [[Succulent plant|succulent]] [[perennial plant]] in the family Asparagaceae, subfamily [[Agavoideae]]. Under the synonym '''''Agave neglecta''''', it is known as '''wild century plant''' and '''Small's agave'''—the latter in honor of its discoverer in Florida, [[John Kunkel Small]].<ref name=Austin/> Naturalized populations in Florida were considered to be a separate species but are now treated as synonymous with ''A. weberi''.

==Description==
''Agave weberi'' is a relatively short suckering species; the leafy trunks are rarely more than 1 m (3 ft) tall. The leaves, which may be arching or reflexed, can be up to 1.6 m (5.2 ft) long and 18 cm (7 in) across. The flowering stalks can reach a height of 8 m (26 ft). The flowers are yellow, up to 8 cm (3 in) long.<ref name=FNA_Aw/><ref name=FNA_An/><ref name=Pois01/>

==Taxonomy==
There has been confusion as to the identity of this species. ''Agave weberi'' was first described in 1901 in a publication authored by [[Jules Poisson]], who attributed the name to [[Jean Francois Cels]].<ref name=IPNI_6788-2/> The description was based on specimens cultivated in Paris, grown from plants originally collected in Mexico, where they were reported to be cultivated for [[fiber]] and to make the alcoholic beverage [[pulque]].<ref name=Pois01/> Later, in 1903, [[John Kunkel Small]] described ''Agave neglecta'',<ref name=IPNI_6601-2/> based on specimens from [[Florida]].<ref name=Smal03/> ''A. neglecta'' has been regarded as [[endemism|endemic]] to [[Florida]], but is now treated as the same species as the Mexican ''A. weberi'' and only naturalized in Florida through human agency.<ref name=ISB/> ''A. weberi'' may be a [[cultivar]] derived from the wild species ''[[Agave vivipara|A. vivipara]]'',<ref name=WCSP_294351/> although an origin from ''[[sisal|A. sisalana]]'' or ''[[Agave kewensis|A. kewensis]]'' has also been suggested.<ref name=FNA_An/>

==Distribution==
The distribution of ''Agave weberi'' is now determined by human activity.<ref name=ISB/> It is believed to have originated in northeastern Mexico (San Luis Potosí, Tamaulipas), and is now naturalized in Texas and Florida in the United States and in the Northern Provinces in South Africa.<ref name=WCSP_294351/> In Florida, it is found in sandy soils, especially near the [[coast]]s.<ref name=FNA_An/>

==Conservation==
Based on the belief that populations in Florida were a separate species, they were the subject of [[habitat conservation|conservation]] concerns.<ref name=FNA_An/><ref name=ISB/>

==Uses==
''Agave weberi'' is cultivated for its value as an [[ornamental plant]], for the production of [[pulque]], and for [[fiber]].<ref name=FNA_Aw/>
